regime_context: The detector shows a broad (14/16 eligible) rotation with Gold Miners as the clear, non-crowded leader (score 2.167, durability 0.85, trend, full breadth) and Silver/Royalties as challenger; gold is the dominant narrative but not one-narrative. The absolute-trend gate is validated for this market (gate_helps true), but cross-sectional momentum has ~no edge and rotation timing is display-only.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver & Royalties can close the margin gap against Gold Miners (score margin currently 0.552); I retire this watch if Silver's durability_bar crosses below 0.70 or the margin widens further above 0.7 instead of narrowing.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the undeniable leader on every coincident leg: top rank, highest durability (0.85, trend-tagged), full breadth (1.0), non-crowded (crowding_z 0.95, flagged false), and a wide margin (0.552) over the challenger. The view is one of narrative persistence, not a return forecast — the trend gate is the only validated edge here and it favours staying with the in-trend leader over shaking out. Momentum rank itself is a focus lens (rank-IC ~0), so this is a structural lean on durability and trend-health.
evidence: durability_bar 0.85, hurst_tag 'trend', breadth 1.0 — healthy, cohesive trend
crowded false — no sizing caution flag
gate_helps true — absolute-trend gate validated as risk control on this market
theses.dissent: Gold leadership can reverse violently via a mean-reverting shake-out in precious metals; the detector's only validated edge is drawdown avoidance, not directional alpha, and a crowded precious-metals complex is prompt to unwind on any hawkish central-bank surprise. Cross-sectional rank-IC on clean sectors is ~0, so even the strongest leader has no momentum return edge.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags the S&P/TSX benchmark by more than 5% over any 20-trading-day window from today

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver is a challenger with a lower score (1.615), lower durability (0.77, mixed), and the rotation margin is wide. It shares the same ETF proxy (XGD.TO) as Gold Miners, so there is no clean separation to overweight; this is a relative-underweight vs the leader, not a fade call. No crowding flag regardless.
evidence: rank 2, score 1.615 vs leader 2.167, margin 0.552 — distant second
durability_bar 0.77, hurst_tag 'mixed' — weaker, less trend-healthy than gold
same ETF proxy XGD.TO — not independently scorable from Gold Miners
theses.dissent: Silver has higher beta to precious-metals upside and could outperform Gold Miners in a strong PM leg; underweighting the runner-up in a broad rotation is arbitrary when the proxy is the same and both are trending.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO (silver proxy) outperforms the Gold Miners leadership leg by over 3% before the check-by date on a theme-basis comparison

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Copper ranks third but is crowded (crowding_z 1.23, crowded true) and durability is mixed (0.76). Crowding is a size-down caution only, never a fade — and since the chart already shows a crowded texture with weaker trend-health, the honest lean is to avoid leaning in either direction. No validated edge supports adding or shorting.
evidence: rank 3, score 1.407 — still positive but fading vs gold/silver
theses.dissent: Copper is the highest-ranked non-precious-metals theme and could benefit from infrastructure/electrification flows independent of gold; avoiding a still-eligible theme forfeits any continuation.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO decrowds (crowding_z crosses below 1) and its score crosses above Silver by more than 0.3

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
